report:
PASS applies to the restricted spherical A–F assertions and the entire new regularity Lemma 2. The continuous-density diagonal, four-term torsion transfer, coordinated transform parameter, kernel derivative estimate and Hölder interpolation establish the previously missing proof edges. The historical candidate=false and first INCONCLUSIVE remain historical records; neither supplies a mathematical premise. Original S15 completion and literature novelty are assessed separately below. No protected artifact was inspected.

1. Local products and conventions. Work throughout with D=i∂∂̄/(2π) and canonical representatives. On a relatively compact coordinate domain put β=D|z|² and choose Tβ≥h. For bounded genuine h-psh b, q=b+T|z|² is bounded psh, and the complete corrected product is
MA_h(b)=Σ_{l=0}^n binom(n,l)(Dq)^l∧(h−Tβ)^{n−l}.
Every term has finite variation on smaller domains by local CLN bounds. Convolution of q, followed by a vanishing positive quadratic correction compensating for convolution of h, gives positive smooth h-Hessians converging to this expression. Smooth algebra and closed-product continuity prove independence of T, coordinate compatibility and locality. This also establishes every lower and mixed product used below through finite local expansions. Uniform convergence of bounded potentials gives product convergence by telescoping and local CLN estimates. A finite cover proves finite mass for each actual bounded potential, and uniform mass bounds for families with a common bound. It makes no assertion about the supremum over all bounded potentials. These applications use the local results of [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), premise 0.

2. Exact radial normalization and complete products. Set s=log|z|², L=Ds and Q=ds∧d^cs on the punctured ball. Then L≥0, Q≥0, L^n=Q²=0, and
(Df(s))^l=(f′)^lL^l+l(f′)^{l−1}f″Q∧L^{l−1}.
For smooth convex increasing f, angular integration of its top product gives d((f′)^n), with normalized Euclidean surface probability as angular measure. Indeed its Euclidean density is (n!/π^n)(f′)^{n−1}f″r^{−2n}; multiplying by the sphere area and dr gives 2n(f′)^{n−1}f″dr/r=d((f′)^n). Convex smoothing therefore proves (D log max(|z|²,r²))^n=σ_r with coefficient exactly one.

For a piecewise constant slope c(s), jumping from B_j to C_j at s_j=log r_j², every lower product is
(Df)^l=c(s)^lL^l+Σ_j(C_j^l−B_j^l)δ(s−s_j)Q∧L^{l−1}.
Here δ(s−s_j)Q∧L^{n−1}=σ_j, and its β-trace in degree l has mass r_j^{2(n−l)}. The ordinary radial trace is (n−l)c(s)^lr^{2(n−l)}ds for l<n. These formulas include all cross terms; they are local closed-current computations.

3. The independent reference. Write a_j=√r_j, q_0=2^{−1/2}, A=Σa_j=√r_0/(√2−1), and S_n=Σa_j^n. Define F=Σa_j log max(|z|²,r_j²), including F(0)=Σa_j log r_j², and G=χF extended by zero. Summability of Σ(1+j)a_j gives uniform convergence and the actual finite continuous value at p. On a fixed annulus outside all spheres every cutoff summand equals χ log|z|². Its largest negative h-eigenvalue supplies the stated finite L_h, giving DG≥−AL_hh. With ε=[2(1+AL_h)]^{−1}, the normalized potential εG−sup_X(εG) satisfies h+Du≥h/2.

The radial slope obeys c(r)=Σ_{r_j<r}a_j≤√r/(1−q_0). Integrating F′(r)=2c(r)/r proves |F(r)−F(t)|≤4(1−q_0)^{−1}√|r−t|, including t=0. Multiplication by χ adds a Lipschitz term. Chart comparison and boundedness for distant pairs give global C^{0,1/2} regularity.

Its slopes at r_j are B_j=q_0a_j/(1−q_0) and C_j=a_j/(1−q_0). Thus C_j^n−B_j^n=A^na_j^n/S_n and (DF)^n=A^nρ. All lower traces are integrable at p because their controlling exponent is 2(n−l)+l/2>0. To exclude a residual origin current, truncate F from below at F(r_N). These decreasing bounded psh truncations are constant inside r_N; the replacement innermost trace is C_N^lr_N^{2(n−l)}→0, also for l=n. Bedford–Taylor convergence proves the formulas across p without an additional term there.

On the inner ball the complete product is Σ_l binom(n,l)ε^lh^{n−l}∧(DF)^l; all terms are positive. On the complement G=Aχ log|z|² is smooth and the product is its ordinary smooth top power. The formulas agree on overlaps. Therefore this reference dominates k_Iρ with k_I=(εA)^n>0 and has finite positive entire mass.

4. The author reference is separately valid. Its actual function is u_0=[χF+A(1−χ)]/Z, where Z=2KA and K≥1 bounds the negative h-Hessian of the common transition function χ log|z|²+1−χ. Consequently h+Du_0≥h/2. The summable series is uniformly convergent, has its canonical series value at p, and is C^{0,1/2}; the displayed logarithmic increment estimate and geometric-tail summation prove this directly. On the inner ball the pure top Hessian is A^nρ/Z^n. Retaining only diagonal terms gives the advertised weaker coefficient k_A=S_n/Z^n. Positivity of the discarded local terms and uniform corrected-product convergence justify that inequality. The complete product and finite mass follow from paragraphs 1–2. Subtracting the supremum preserves both. The two constructions differ by their scaling and by the author's smooth A(1−χ)/Z term. Their potentials, currents and advertised constants need not coincide, and no ordering between k_A and k_I is established.

5. A and C. Each σ_j is the product of a bounded local psh clipped logarithm. Scaling that function into [0,1] and using pluripolar capacity zero proves σ_j(P)=0 for every locally pluripolar Borel P. Countable additivity proves the same for ρ. Its mass is one; the countable sphere union has zero smooth volume and full ρ-mass. None of the spheres contains p, so ρ({p})=0 despite accumulation. No weak-limit preservation assertion is involved. If M=M_ρ(ν)<∞, then 0<ν(X)≤M<∞ and ν≤Mρ. Thus ν is non-pluripolar and the same normalized author reference satisfies MA_h(u_ρ)≥(k_A/M)ν. This includes arbitrary bounded measurable densities, with no lower bound or smooth-volume density.

6. The density diagonal repairs the genuine approximation defect. Put α=MA_h(u_ρ) and ν=C_0gα, 0≤g≤1. Continuous clipped g_l→g in L¹(α) exist by Radon regularity. The root inequality and Jensen give g_l^{1/n}→g^{1/n} in L¹(α). Choose smooth genuine reference approximants converging uniformly, with a common smaller Hölder bound. A diagonal against g_l^{1/n}, and g_l times each of the first l members of a dense continuous test family, gives ν_l=C_0g_lMA_h(v_l)⇀ν and inf_l∫g_l^{1/n}MA_h(v_l)>0 after discarding finitely many indices. Common reference masses handle approximation of arbitrary continuous tests.

This works for the singular datum. By contrast, the sphere-union indicator times every smooth reference product is zero, although its product with the limiting reference need not be zero. Thus the original fixed-Borel multiplication shortcut remains invalid. The author's diagonal and n9's independently constructed smooth-density diagonal both address it. The explicit references also admit local convolution approximants preserving a strict margin, so this specialized construction does not depend solely on an abstract approximation citation. The relevant [KN2018](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.3232.pdf) statements are premises 1–4; the diagonal is a new proof argument.

7. Approximate homogeneous solutions and uniform bounds. Each ν_l has a continuous nonnegative smooth-volume density of positive integral, so premise 6 gives sup φ_l=0 and MA_h(φ_l)=c_lν_l. Apply the smooth-volume mixed inequality with the actual reference density, including where it vanishes. It yields
c_l^{1/n}C_0^{1/n}∫g_l^{1/n}MA_h(v_l)≤∫h_{φ_l}∧h_{v_l}^{n−1}.
Integration by parts expresses the last integral using fixed torsion and weighted lower reference products. Weighted CLN bounds it uniformly before oscillation bounds for φ_l are available. For references with a common bound, shift and divide them into [0,1]; positive expansions control the lower products as well. Hence c_l is bounded above.

The common smaller Hölder norm and domination constants give a common exponential capacity bound for MA_h(φ_l), hence one admissible capacity function. Fix the comparison parameter and a sufficiently small level s once. Premise 7 gives cap_h{φ_l<inf φ_l+s}≤Cc_lν_l(X)/s^n and s≤κ of that capacity, with κ(t)→0 at zero. Since ν_l(X) is uniformly bounded, c_l is bounded away from zero. The same lower capacity bound, combined with the normalized sublevel-capacity estimate, bounds ||φ_l||∞. No uniform L^p norm of the approximating densities is used. These are exact applications of [KN13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491v2) and [Nguyen](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891v1), premises 6–9.

8. Four-term torsion transfer and the continuous exact limit. For uniformly bounded genuine a,b,r,t put f=|a−b|=2max(a,b)−a−b and T=Σ_{k=0}^{n−1}h_r^k∧h_t^{n−1−k}. Local corrected algebra gives MA_h(r)−MA_h(t)=D(r−t)∧T. Integration by parts retains
D(fT)=Df∧T+df∧d^cT−d^cf∧dT+fDT.
The first term is a signed combination of bounded positive Hessian products. The two gradient terms have bounded variation by local gradient CLN and Cauchy–Schwarz. The last term contains fixed smooth Dh and dh∧d^ch multiplied by lower bounded products, so its variation is bounded as well. All constants depend only on the common bounds and fixed geometry. Local decreasing regularization justifies the identities for bounded canonical representatives. Consequently the asserted transfer bound C||r−t||∞ holds. No torsion term is discarded.

Extract c_l→c>0 and φ_l→φ in L¹ and almost everywhere in smooth volume. The uniformly bounded canonical limit has sup φ=0. Premise 10 supplies, after a countable diagonal, L¹ convergence against every fixed reference product. For a fixed large reference index m, the transfer estimate bounds the change from that product to MA_h(v_j) by C||v_j−v_m||∞. Uniform reference convergence therefore gives the two-index error ∫|φ_j−φ_k|MA_h(v_j)→0. Domination transfers this to each solution measure. Applying stability in both directions proves a uniformly Cauchy subsequence. Its continuous genuine limit satisfies MA_h(φ)=cν by uniform corrected-product continuity, with exact mass cν(X). Stability constants here are used for uniformly bounded normalized families, not arbitrary downward constant shifts. This independently establishes the continuous exact equation needed as Lemma 2's antecedent.

9. The earlier exponent defect is real, and the new parameter proof repairs it. The printed bound Cδ^{αα_1}, with α_1<1, cannot be strengthened to Cδ^α in the old minimizer argument. Dividing by a level comparable to δ^α gives an unbounded logarithmic estimate rather than a uniform minimizer scale. The first review correctly left that edge unresolved; n2 and n7's final theorem citation did not repair it.

For the new lemma fix its continuous normalized exact solution φ, let M=||φ||∞, and use the imported exponents η,γ∈(0,1). Set q=ηγ/2, ε=δ^q and b=(ε−2Kδ)/A. For small δ, ε/(2A)≤b≤ε/A. The transform F satisfies h+DF≥−εh; T=(1−ε)F therefore satisfies h+DT≥ε²h. Monotonicity gives φ≤F≤R_δφ+2Kδ. The logarithmic penalty uniformly excludes t near zero for fixed δ,b, so the minimum is attained and F is continuous.

Choose B≥M+2K+1. Since R_δφ≤0, ψ=T−Bε is continuous, genuine h-psh and nonpositive, with a uniform bound. Crucially,
ψ−φ≤(1−ε)(R_δφ−φ+2Kδ)+ε(M−B).
The subtraction occurs before taking the stability power. Thus ||(ψ−φ)_+||_{L¹(μ)}≤Cδ^η, and sup(T−φ)≤Cδ^{ηγ}+Bε≤C_1ε. Because φ≤0, 0≤F−φ≤2C_1ε. At a minimizer t_0, monotonicity gives b log(δ/t_0)≤F−φ. Hence t_0≥κδ, κ=exp(−4AC_1)>0 independent of point and radius. Another monotonicity application and rescaling yield ||R_rφ−φ||∞≤Cr^q. Every curvature, continuity and stability antecedent is established here.

10. Kernel derivative and Hölder interpolation. The formal holomorphic jet used in the regularization is represented by an actual smooth map with exph_z(0)=z and fiber derivative the identity; this is verified in [Demailly, Proposition 2.9](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/regularization_flow.pdf), premise 5. In coordinates, the map (exph_z(rξ)−z)/r extends smoothly to r=0 with value ξ. The parameterized inverse function theorem, smooth metric density and flat smooth cutoff therefore give
K_r(z,y)=r^{−2n}a(z,(y−z)/r,r),
where a has common bounded first derivatives and fixed bounded fiber support on a finite chart cover. Differentiation gives ∫|∇_zK_r|dy≤C/r, hence ||∇R_rφ||∞≤CM/r. For distance s,
|φ(x)−φ(y)|≤2Cr^q+CMs/r.
Choosing r=s^{1/(1+q)} proves C^{0,q/(1+q)} regularity; boundedness handles larger distances. This verifies the whole general lemma with a positive exponent. It uses neither the defective printed minimizer step nor the final Hölder range conclusion. Applying it to paragraph 8 establishes D.

11. Exact exponential existence and its support. Domination gives the actual identity ν=fα with a bounded Borel representative 0≤f≤M/k_A; its value is zero α-a.e. on excess reference parts. The form h is semipositive and genuinely big using the strict smooth potential 0. Thus the precise hypotheses of [ALS Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1), premise 11, hold for every specified λ>0.

Its support is valid in this application. Bounded smooth-obstacle envelopes have contact support. If an obstacle is only ω-psh for h≤ω, compare the envelope and obstacle in the larger ω background and then use contact support: MA_h(P_h(a))≤1_contact MA_ω(a). This proves the needed bounded smooth-volume density; the same-background Proposition 2.4 alone is not a larger-background theorem. Premises 13–14 then supply the approximate exponential equations. A finite measure of mass m is converted from the probability theorem by the shift −(log m)/λ. For the explicit reference one can also use its smooth strict approximants directly.

For a fixed positive smooth multiplier, exponential comparison with reference shifts gives uniform bounds. Uniform reference convergence, fixed-measure convergence and the transfer estimate verify the varying-reference integral error. For a general bounded multiplier, approximate it by uniformly bounded positive smooth functions in L¹(α), and establish the mixed inequality first at the actual smooth-volume reference approximants. In the upper-bound argument the normalized v_j need not initially be uniformly bounded below. Instead apply fixed-measure convergence to e^{λv_j/n}: these are bounded genuine quasi-psh functions for one fixed enlarged background, since D(e^{av_j})≥−ah for v_j≤0. Their limiting reference integral against f^{1/n} is positive because v is finite α-a.e. and f is nonzero. Weighted CLN then bounds c_j^{1/n}, where c_j=e^{λsup u_j}, and hence bounds sup u_j. A shifted reference supplies the uniform lower bound. This checks the previously premature boundedness application.

12. Bounded-rooftop convergence, exactness and uniqueness. For the resulting uniformly bounded family, P_h(inf u_j) lies between constants and is equivalent to 0. Every bounded h-psh b belongs to the task's E_env(X,h,0): for each t≥1 choose the genuine constant witness t inf_X b. The zero model is available in every smaller semipositive background. Uniform finite masses follow from paragraph 1. Thus premise 12 uses its bounded-rooftop alternative without v_−>0.

Its bounded argument can also be checked directly. After making the weighted errors summable, finite rooftop contact inequalities bound the error for each tail rooftop by the sum of tail errors. Decreasing bounded-product convergence passes to the infinite tail rooftop; increasing convergence passes to its limit. The latter agrees with u almost everywhere for its own product. Bounded domination with coefficient zero then forces equality everywhere. Monotone lower rooftops and upper tail envelopes squeeze u_j to u in capacity. Uniformly bounded mixed measures are uniformly capacity dominated; applying this domination to {|u_j−u|>ε} and telescoping against smooth tests proves corrected-product convergence in capacity, including every torsion term. Quasicontinuity handles fixed bounded weights. For the final fixed reference, ||f_je^{λu_j}−fe^{λu}||_{L¹(α)}→0. Hence the limiting exponential equation is exact.

Every Hermitian h satisfies the finite torsion bounds and is individually non-collapsing, as checked in [Guedj–Lu](https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf), premise 15. This means positive mass for each bounded potential, not a positive infimum. For two bounded solutions x,y, on {x<y−δ} one has MA_h(x)≤e^{−λδ}MA_h(y−δ). Strict-coefficient domination gives x≥y−δ; let δ↓0 and exchange x,y. Uniqueness holds at every canonical point, including off supp ν. Finally
0<e^{λinf U}ν(X)≤MA_h(U)(X)≤e^{λsup U}ν(X)<∞.
The fixed scalar allows no further sup-zero normalization. This establishes E.

13. F, numerical covariance and harmless corrections. If D_source=sD, the author's method uses reference u/s, source exponent sλ, and output multiplied by s. The independent method scales h and ν to sh and s^nν while retaining potentials and λ. Both preserve the requested equation exactly. Bedford–Taylor's operator is 4πD; the published GL2 operator is 2πD. The manuscript's approximation citation should read KN Lemma 2.3, and its capacity citation Lemma 2.1/Corollary 2.2; these are harmless swapped references. The exact torsion coefficient in D(h_ψ^{n−1}) is (n−1)(n−2), and zero-coefficient terms are omitted in low dimensions. Nguyen Proposition 1.5's auxiliary small-torsion hypothesis can be met using a fixed sufficiently enlarged auxiliary metric; alternatively the needed bounded-family estimates already follow locally from paragraph 1. The source's auxiliary exponential sublevel factor is e^{λt/n}; positivity also follows directly from α-a.e. finiteness. Compactness arguments require subsequence extraction. These bookkeeping clarifications do not alter a conclusion. The density diagonal and parameter proof are substantial new arguments, independently checked here.

Neither mass invariant is used. Consequently the construction and exact equations apply to any given h with v_−=0 or v_+=∞. This does not exhibit a manifold having either exceptional invariant. Finiteness comes from actual bounded products and exact finite targets.

14. Entire returned DAG and comparison. All ten public nodes and their 24 actual edges were checked. With an arrow meaning 'uses', the unchanged DAG is:
n1: []; n2: []; n3: []; n4: [];
n5→n1;
n6→n1,n5;
n7→n2,n5,n6;
n8→n3,n4,n5,n6,n7;
n9→n1,n2,n5,n6;
n10→n1,n2,n3,n4,n5,n6,n7,n8,n9.
The leaves are external-source nodes, not task grants. n5's full corrected and radial products, n6's distinct reference, n7's normalization, n8's exponential application and n9's diagnostic/diagonal are valid. n2/n7 alone did not reconstruct the regularity branch; paragraphs 6–10 now do so. n10's original-scope and overlap reservations remain appropriate.

The complete additional proof DAG is: premise 0→local corrected products, radial normalization and capacity-continuity argument; these plus cutoff geometry→both genuine references→A,B; references plus measure comparison→C and the RN datum. For D: references, premise 2 and the density diagonal→approximate data; premise 6→approximate solutions; premises 8–9→upper coefficient bound; premises 2 and 7→lower coefficient and oscillation bounds; premise 0 and 8→four-term transfer; premise 10 plus transfer→two-index error; premise 3→uniform Cauchy convergence; premise 0→continuous exact equation. That equation plus premises 2–5→the coordinated transform and kernel proof→Lemma 2→D. For E: RN datum and strict smooth bigness→premise 11; its checked support is premises 13–14→smooth-obstacle equations, premises 8–10 and transfer→mixed bounds and convergence, premises 12 and 15→bounded-rooftop convergence, premise 0→actual product limit, and premise 15→uniqueness. Exact equations and boundedness→their mass and normalization assertions. Geometry and measure comparison→the stated intrinsic sufficient condition. No other proof dependency is required.

15. Separate original S15 and novelty judgment. The test is non-tautological: it quantifies only over explicit geometric measure data, not potentials. For a fixed transported ρ its meaning is unchanged by descriptions; existence of some transported coordinate configuration is biholomorphically invariant. Different predetermined references need not give the same class. Every nonzero admissible ν is substantively singular. This establishes the mathematical sufficient-condition branch allowed by the original criterion and distinguishes its three equations with their correct classes and normalizations. It gives no conclusion at M_ρ=∞, necessary classification, optimal coefficient, prescribed mass, unbounded exponential uniqueness, prescribed-type classification or P11 result. The analytic range implications substantially overlap KN2018 and ALS. Novelty of the explicit geometric criterion and repairs is not established by this comparison. Accordingly full original S15 completion and literature priority are not certified; their status remains separate from this restricted PASS.

passages.statement: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on coordinate domains, closed Bedford–Taylor mixed Hessian products are positive, symmetric and multilinear, and their products, bounded-function-weighted products and gradient products have the stated decreasing-limit continuity. Local masses and gradient energies satisfy CLN bounds on compact subsets. Psh functions are locally quasicontinuous, and monotone psh convergence is locally quasi-uniform. On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain, pluripolar sets are exactly the sets of zero outer Bedford–Taylor capacity. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity, Theorems 2.1, 2.4, 2.7, 2.10, 3.5, 6.9 and 7.2, and Corollary 2.2.

Let φ,ψ be bounded ω-psh, φ≤0, −1≤ψ≤0, 0<ε<1, m=inf_X[φ−(1−ε)ψ] and U(ε,s)={φ<(1−ε)ψ+m+s}. For increments in the stated torsion-dependent small interval, modified comparison gives [(1−ε)t]^ncap_ω(U(ε,s))≤C∫_{U(ε,s+4(1−ε)t)}MA_ω(φ). If MA_ω(φ)(E)≤F_H(cap_ω(E)), F_H(x)=x/H(x^{−1/n}), with increasing H>0 and ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^{1/n}]<∞, then sufficiently small D satisfies D≤κ(cap_ω(U(ε,D))), where κ(t)→0 at zero. Normalized ω-psh functions have a uniform L¹ bound and L¹ compactness, and cap_ω{φ<−T}≤C/T. Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:1312.5491v2, Theorem 5.3, Lemma 5.4 and the estimates used in Corollary 5.6.

For increments in the stated torsion-dependent small interval, modified comparison gives [(1−ε)t]^ncap_ω(U(ε,s))≤C∫_{U(ε,s+4(1−ε)t)}MA_ω(φ). If MA_ω(φ)(E)≤F_H(cap_ω(E)), F_H(x)=x/H(x^{−1/n}), with increasing H>0 and ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^{1/n}]<∞, then sufficiently small D satisfies D≤κ(cap_ω(U(ε,D))), where κ(t)→0 at zero. For smooth semipositive ω of positive volume, the two-sided bounds −Bω²≤dd^cω≤Bω² and −Bω³≤dω∧d^cω≤Bω³ imply individual non-collapse: each bounded genuine ω-psh product has positive mass. For a non-collapsing ω and bounded genuine ω-psh u,v, MA_ω(u)≤cMA_ω(v) on {u<v}, 0≤c<1, implies u≥v. Consequently e^{−λv}MA_ω(v)≥e^{−λu}MA_ω(u) implies v≤u for λ>0. Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2, Corollary 1.6, Proposition 2.8 and Corollary 2.9.

premises: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on coordinate domains, closed Bedford–Taylor mixed Hessian products are positive, symmetric and multilinear, and their products, bounded-function-weighted products and gradient products have the stated decreasing-limit continuity. Local masses and gradient energies satisfy CLN bounds on compact subsets. Psh functions are locally quasicontinuous, and monotone psh convergence is locally quasi-uniform. On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain, pluripolar sets are exactly the sets of zero outer Bedford–Taylor capacity. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity, Theorems 2.1, 2.4, 2.7, 2.10, 3.5, 6.9 and 7.2, and Corollary 2.2.

On a compact Hermitian manifold, a positive Radon measure μ with 0<μ(X)<∞ admits a Hölder continuous ω-psh φ and c>0 with MA_ω(φ)=cμ if and only if μ≤C_0MA_ω(v) for a global Hölder ω-psh v and C_0>0. Kołodziej–Nguyen 2018, Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.3.

On a compact Hermitian manifold, C^{0,α} ω-psh functions admit smooth ω-psh approximants converging in C^{0,α′} for 0<α′<α<1. Hermitian capacity is locally comparable to Bedford–Taylor capacity. Measures dominated by Hölder-reference products satisfy exponential capacity bounds and μ(E)≤C_τcap_ω(E)^{1+τ}; fixed domination and reference Hölder bounds give common constants. Kołodziej–Nguyen 2018, Lemmas 2.1 and 2.3 and Corollary 2.2.

For bounded ω-psh φ, its normalized Chern regularization R_t has R_tφ+Kt² increasing in t. Its transform F_{δ,b}=inf_{0<t≤δ}(R_tφ+Kt²+Kt−b log(t/δ)) satisfies ω+dd^cF_{δ,b}≥−(Ab+2Kδ)ω. If μ is dominated by a Hölder-reference product, ||R_δφ−φ||_{L¹(μ)}≤Cδ^η for some η∈(0,1). Kołodziej–Nguyen 2018, equations (2.7)–(2.8) and Lemmas 2.7–2.8.
